declare module 'harness-dsl' {
  import { z } from 'zod';
  import type * as K from 'harness-dsl/kernel';

  type Shape = z.ZodRawShape;
  type Obj<S extends Shape> = z.infer<z.ZodObject<S>>;
  type ScalarShape = { [key: string]: z.ZodType<K.Scalar> };
  type NumberKeys<A> = { [P in keyof A]-?: A[P] extends number ? P : never }[keyof A] & string;
  type Active<St> = Extract<St, { readonly position: 'active' }>;
  type Settled<St> = Exclude<St, { readonly position: 'active' }>;

  export type Position = K.Position;
  export type Verdict = K.Verdict;
  export type Scalar = K.Scalar;
  export type Duration = K.Duration;
  export type Window = K.Window;
  export type Create<A, F> = K.Create<A, F>;
  export type Supply<A, F, Ev> = K.Supply<A, F, Ev>;
  export type SupplyMaker<A, F, Ev> = K.SupplyMaker<A, F, Ev>;
  export type EnvRef = K.EnvRef;
  export type PortRef = K.PortRef;
  export type Secret = K.Secret;
  export type Account = K.Account;
  export type Model = K.Model;
  export type QuotaPartition = K.QuotaPartition;
  export type Runner = K.Runner;
  export type Store = K.Store;
  export type MemoryStore = K.MemoryStore;
  export type Ledger = K.Ledger;
  export type Supplier<Out> = K.Supplier<Out>;
  export type Projection = K.Projection;
  export type Client = K.Client;
  export type Executable<I, O> = K.Executable<I, O>;
  export type External<I, O> = K.External<I, O>;
  export type Recurrence = K.Recurrence;
  export type Intent = K.Intent;

  export interface State<N extends string = string, P extends K.Position = K.Position> extends K.StateSpec {
    readonly entity: 'state';
    readonly name: N;
    readonly position: P;
  }

  export interface TimerSource<A> {
    attribute<Q extends NumberKeys<A>>(key: Q): K.AttributeTime;
  }

  export interface KindRef<A, F, St extends State, Ev> extends K.KindLike<A> {
    readonly entity: 'work';
    readonly types?: { attributes: A; fields: F; state: St; events: Ev };
  }

  export interface WorkKind<A = {}, F = {}, St extends State = never, Ev = {}, Tm extends string = never, Fl extends State = never>
    extends KindRef<A, F, St, Ev> {
    readonly types?: { attributes: A; fields: F; state: St; events: Ev; timers: Tm; failure: Fl };
    attributes<S extends ScalarShape>(shape: S): WorkKind<Obj<S>, F, St, Ev, Tm, Fl>;
    fields<S extends Shape>(shape: S): WorkKind<A, Obj<S>, St, Ev, Tm, Fl>;
    states<T extends State>(states: readonly T[]): WorkKind<A, F, T, Ev, Tm, never>;
    failsTo<S extends Settled<St>>(state: S): WorkKind<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, S>;
    events<M extends { [name: string]: Shape }>(events: M): WorkKind<A, F, St, { [N in keyof M]: Obj<M[N]> }, Tm, Fl>;
    timers<T extends { [name: string]: K.Timing }>(make: (t: TimerSource<A>) => T): WorkKind<A, F, St, Ev, Tm | (keyof T & string), Fl>;
    key(make: (unit: { attributes: A; fields: F }) => string): WorkKind<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Fl>;
  }

  export interface Role<I = { task: string }, O = { text: string }> extends K.RoleSpec {
    readonly entity: 'role';
    readonly types?: { input: I; output: O };
    intents(intents: readonly K.Intent[]): Role<I, O>;
    instructions(text: string): Role<I, O>;
    input<S extends Shape>(shape: S): Role<Obj<S>, O>;
    output<S extends Shape>(shape: S): Role<I, Obj<S>>;
  }

  export interface Resource extends K.Named {
    readonly entity: 'resource';
    readonly globs: readonly string[];
    paths(globs: readonly string[]): Resource;
  }

  export interface MemoryKind extends K.MemoryKindSpec {
    readonly entity: 'memory';
    curated(): MemoryKind;
  }

  export interface Playbook extends K.PlaybookSpec {
    readonly entity: 'playbook';
    store(store: K.MemoryStore): Playbook;
    recall(policy: K.RecallPolicy): Playbook;
  }

  export interface Decision<D> extends K.DecisionSpec {
    readonly entity: 'decision';
    readonly types?: { decision: D };
  }

  export interface Command<D = null> extends K.Executable<K.CommandInput, K.CommandResult<D>>, K.CommandSpec {
    readonly executable: 'command';
    parses<S extends Shape>(shape: S): Command<Obj<S>>;
  }

  export interface Pool extends K.Named {
    readonly entity: 'pool';
    accounts(entries: readonly { account: K.Account; share: number }[]): Pool;
    prefer(policy: K.AccountPolicy): Pool;
    fallback(account: K.Account): Pool;
  }

  export interface Agent<I, O> extends K.Executable<I, O> {
    readonly executable: 'agent';
    readonly role: Role<I, O>;
    model(model: K.Model | K.ChoicePolicy<K.Model>): Agent<I, O>;
    pool(pool: Pool | K.Account): Agent<I, O>;
    recalls(playbooks: readonly Playbook[]): Agent<I, O>;
    records(playbook: Playbook): Agent<I, O>;
    leaseWrites(): Agent<I, O>;
    mustPass(check: K.CommandSpec): Agent<I, O>;
  }

  export interface Retry extends K.RetrySpec { readonly entity: 'retry' }

  export type Restart = 'rerun' | 'ask' | 'escalate' | { readonly probe: Command<{ readonly done: boolean }> };

  export interface StepOptions {
    readonly retry?: Retry;
    readonly timeoutMs?: number;
    readonly onFailure?: 'fail' | 'halt';
    readonly runner?: K.Runner;
    readonly restart?: Restart;
  }

  export interface FlowContext<In, P, Out, Ev> {
    readonly input: In;
    readonly params: P;
    readonly out: Out;
    readonly events: { readonly [N in keyof Ev]: readonly K.Received<Ev[N]>[] };
    readonly unit: K.UnitView;
    readonly attempt: K.AttemptView;
  }
  export interface LoopRound<C> { readonly round: number; readonly carry: C | null }
  type Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X> = FlowContext<In, P, Out, Ev> & X;

  export interface Flow<In, P, Out, Sp, L extends string, Ev, Hl> extends K.FlowSpec {
    readonly entity: 'flow';
    readonly types?: { input: In; params: P; out: Out; spawns: Sp; ends: L; events: Ev; halts: Hl };
  }

  export interface FlowDraft<In, P, Out, Sp, L extends string, Ev, Hl, X> extends K.Named {
    readonly entity: 'flow-draft';
    requires<S extends Shape>(shape: S): FlowDraft<Obj<S>, P, Out, Sp, L, Ev, Hl, X>;
    params<S extends Shape>(shape: S): FlowDraft<In, Obj<S>, Out, Sp, L, Ev, Hl, X>;
    events<E extends { [name: string]: Shape }>(events: E): FlowDraft<In, P, Out, Sp, L, { [N in keyof E]: Obj<E[N]> }, Hl, X>;
    step<Q extends string, I, O>(
      key: Q,
      executable: K.Executable<I, O>,
      input: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => NoInfer<I>,
      options?: StepOptions,
    ): FlowDraft<In, P, Out & { [R in Q]: O }, Sp, L, Ev, Hl, X>;
    batch<Q extends string, I, O>(
      key: Q,
      agent: Agent<I, O>,
      items: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => readonly NoInfer<I>[],
      options?: StepOptions,
    ): FlowDraft<In, P, Out & { [R in Q]: readonly O[] }, Sp, L, Ev, Hl, X>;
    halt<Q extends string, D>(
      key: Q,
      decision: Decision<D>,
      spec: { ask: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => string },
    ): FlowDraft<In, P, Out & { [R in Q]: D }, Sp, L, Ev, Hl & { [R in Q]: D }, X>;
    spawn<Q extends string, S extends Shape>(
      key: Q,
      spec: { child: S; items: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => readonly Obj<S>[] },
    ): FlowDraft<In, P, Out & { [R in Q]: readonly K.ChildView[] }, Sp & { [R in Q]: Obj<S> }, L, Ev, Hl, X>;
    loop<Q extends string, C extends Shape, B>(
      key: Q,
      spec: { carry: C; rounds: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => number },
      body: (round: FlowDraft<In, P, Out, Sp, L, Ev, Hl, X & LoopRound<Obj<C>>>) => FlowDraft<In, P, B, Sp, L, Ev, Hl, X & LoopRound<Obj<C>>>,
      again: (last: B, c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => Obj<C> | null,
    ): FlowDraft<In, P, Out & { [R in Q]: { rounds: number; last: B; exhausted: boolean } }, Sp, L, Ev, Hl, X>;
    sets<S extends ScalarShape>(shape: S, make: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => Obj<S>): FlowDraft<In & Obj<S>, P, Out, Sp, L, Ev, Hl, X>;
    exit<E extends string>(label: E, when: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => boolean): FlowDraft<In, P, Out, Sp, L | E, Ev, Hl, X>;
    ends<E extends string>(labels: readonly E[], pick: (c: Ctx<In, P, Out, Ev, X>) => NoInfer<E>): Flow<In, P, Out, Sp, L | E, Ev, Hl>;
  }

  export interface Reaction<To extends State, Fr extends State = never> extends K.ReactionSpec {
    readonly entity: 'reaction';
    readonly to: To;
    readonly fromStates: readonly Fr[];
    from<S extends State>(states: readonly S[]): Reaction<To, Fr | S>;
    cancels(): Reaction<To, Fr>;
  }

  export interface Skip<A, D> {
    readonly name: string;
    readonly when: (c: K.GateContext<A>) => boolean;
    readonly decision: D;
  }

  export type Route<S> = S | { readonly to: S; readonly upTo: number; readonly then: S };

  type HandlerConfig<A, F, St extends State, Fl extends State, Ev, In, P, Out, Sp, L extends string, FEv, Hl> =
    { ends: { [Q in L]: Route<Settled<St>> } } &
    ([Active<St>] extends [never] ? {} : { opens: Active<St>; during?: { [Q in keyof Out & string]?: Active<St> } }) &
    ([Fl] extends [never] ? { exhausted: Settled<St> } : {}) &
    ({} extends P ? { params?: P } : { params: P }) &
    ({} extends Sp ? {} : { spawns: { [Q in keyof Sp]: (child: Sp[Q]) => K.NewUnit } }) &
    { skips?: { [Q in keyof Hl]?: Skip<A, Hl[Q]> } } &
    ([A & F] extends [In] ? {} : { unitDoesNotSatisfyFlowInput: never }) &
    ([Ev] extends [FEv] ? {} : { kindLacksFlowEvents: never });

  export interface Lane<A, F, St extends State, Ev, Tm extends string, Fl extends State, Out> extends K.LaneLike<A> {
    readonly entity: 'lane';
    readonly types?: { attributes: A; fields: F; state: St; events: Ev; timers: Tm; failure: Fl; out: Out };
    supply(suppliers: readonly K.Supplier<K.Supply<A, F, Ev>>[]): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Fl, Out>;
    store(store: K.Store): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Fl, Out>;
    handler<In, P, O, Sp, L extends string, FEv, Hl>(
      flow: Flow<In, P, O, Sp, L, FEv, Hl>,
      config: NoInfer<HandlerConfig<A, F, St, Fl, Ev, In, P, O, Sp, L, FEv, Hl>>,
    ): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Fl, O>;
    runner(runner: K.Runner): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Fl, Out>;
    preflight(check: K.CommandSpec): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Fl, Out>;
    wip(max: number): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Fl, Out>;
    retry(policy: Retry): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Fl, Out>;
    budget(budget: { maxUsdPerUnit: number; onExceed: 'halt' | 'fail' }): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Fl, Out>;
    reacts(reactions: { [N in (keyof Ev & string) | Tm]?: Reaction<St, St> }): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Fl, Out>;
    unit(create: K.Create<A, F>): K.NewUnit;
    event<N extends keyof Ev & string>(key: string, name: N, payload: Ev[N]): K.UnitEvent;
  }

  export interface Source<E> {
    readonly entity: 'source';
    readonly types?: { event: E };
  }

  export interface Trigger<E> extends K.TriggerSpec {
    where(test: (event: E) => boolean): Trigger<E>;
    creates(make: (event: E) => K.NewUnit | readonly K.NewUnit[]): Trigger<E>;
    sends(make: (event: E) => K.UnitEvent | readonly K.UnitEvent[]): Trigger<E>;
    records(playbook: Playbook, make: (event: E) => readonly K.MemoryDraft[]): Trigger<E>;
    invokes<I, O>(executable: K.Executable<I, O>, make: (event: E) => NoInfer<I>): Trigger<E>;
    pauses(lane: K.LaneLike<unknown>): Trigger<E>;
    resumes(lane: K.LaneLike<unknown>): Trigger<E>;
  }

  export interface Metric extends K.MetricSpec { readonly entity: 'metric' }
  export interface MetricHit<T extends unknown[]> { hit(test: (...args: T) => boolean): Metric }
  export interface MetricDraft {
    of<A, F, St extends State, Ev, Tm extends string, Fl extends State, O>(lane: Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Fl, O>): MetricHit<[event: K.TransitionEvent<A, O>]>;
    of<D>(decision: Decision<D>): MetricHit<[decision: D, fact: K.DecisionFact]>;
    of<I, O>(executable: K.Executable<I, O>): MetricHit<[output: O, invocation: K.InvocationView]>;
    invocations(sorts?: readonly K.InvocationView['sort'][]): MetricHit<[invocation: K.InvocationView]>;
  }

  export interface ThresholdSpec {
    readonly window: K.Duration;
    readonly minSamples: number;
    readonly trips: K.Bound;
    readonly resets: K.Bound;

    readonly entity: 'threshold';
    readonly types?: { group: G };
  }

  export interface Operation extends K.OperationSpec { readonly entity: 'operation' }
  export interface OperationDraft<I> extends K.Named {
    input<S extends Shape>(shape: S): OperationDraft<Obj<S>>;

    env(name: string): K.EnvRef;

    state: {
      <N extends string, P extends 'pending' | 'active' | 'waiting'>(name: N, position: P): State<N, P>;

    ): Lane<A, F, St, Ev, Tm, Fl, {}>;

    supply: {

        kind: KindRef<A, F, St, Ev>,

import { H } from 'harness-dsl';

const Queued = H.state('Queued', 'pending');
const Building = H.state('Building', 'active');
const Stalled = H.state('Stalled', 'waiting');
const Done = H.state('Done', 'terminal', 'success');
const Abandoned = H.state('Abandoned', 'terminal', 'failure');
const ticketStates = [Queued, Building, Stalled, Done, Abandoned];

const Proposed = H.state('Proposed', 'pending');
const Planning = H.state('Planning', 'active');
const Underway = H.state('Underway', 'active');
const Delivered = H.state('Delivered', 'terminal', 'success');

const Due = H.state('Due', 'pending');
const Probing = H.state('Probing', 'active');
const Healthy = H.state('Healthy', 'terminal', 'success');
const Unhealthy = H.state('Unhealthy', 'terminal', 'failure');

const ticketAttributes = { ref: z.string(), title: z.string(), area: z.string() };
const ticketFields = { description: z.string() };

const Bug = H.work('bug')
  .attributes(ticketAttributes)
  .fields(ticketFields)
  .states(ticketStates)
  .key(u => u.attributes.ref);

const Feature = H.work('feature')
  .attributes(ticketAttributes)
  .fields(ticketFields)
  .states(ticketStates)
  .key(u => u.attributes.ref);

const Epic = H.work('epic')
  .attributes({ ref: z.string(), title: z.string() })
  .fields({ description: z.string() })
  .states([Proposed, Planning, Underway, Stalled, Delivered, Abandoned])
  .key(u => u.attributes.ref);

const Heartbeat = H.work('service-heartbeat')
  .attributes({ service: z.string(), at: z.number() })
  .states([Due, Probing, Healthy, Unhealthy])
  .failsTo(Unhealthy)
  .key(u => `${u.attributes.service}@${u.attributes.at}`);

const subscriptionA = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-a', { configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_CONFIG_A') });
const subscriptionB = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-b', { configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_CONFIG_B') });
const subscriptionC = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-c', { configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_CONFIG_C') });
const apiAccount = anthropic.account('anthropic-api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') });

const soonestExpiring = H.policy.account('soonest-expiring-first', c =>
  c.eligible.slice().sort((a, b) => a.windowEndsAt - b.windowEndsAt)[0] ?? null);

const claudePool = H.pool('claude-subscriptions')
  .accounts([
    { account: subscriptionA, share: 0.5 },
    { account: subscriptionB, share: 0.3 },
    { account: subscriptionC, share: 0.2 },
  ])
  .prefer(soonestExpiring)
  .fallback(apiAccount);

const sonnet = claudeCode.model('claude-sonnet-4-5');
const opus = claudeCode.model('claude-opus-4-1');

const builderModel = H.policy.model('builder-cheap-until-it-slips', [sonnet, opus], c => {
  const cheap = c.metrics.success({ kind: c.unit?.kind, model: sonnet, window: { days: 14 } });
  if (cheap.n < 20) return sonnet;
  return cheap.rate !== null && cheap.rate < 0.85 ? opus : sonnet;
});

const trackRate = (x: { track: { present: number; succeeded: number } }) =>
  (x.track.succeeded + 1) / (x.track.present + 2);

const specificThenProven = H.policy.recall('specific-then-proven', c =>
  c.candidates
    .slice()
    .sort((a, b) => b.specificity - a.specificity || trackRate(b) - trackRate(a))
    .slice(0, c.limit));

const experience = H.playbook('coding-experience', H.memory.experience('coding-experience').curated())
  .store(jsonl.memory('.harness/memory/experience.jsonl'))
  .recall(specificThenProven);

  .store(jsonl.memory('.harness/memory/taste.jsonl'))
  .recall(specificThenProven);

  .output({ summary: z.string() });

const auditorRole = H.role('auditor')
  .intents(['read', 'execute', 'remember'])
  .instructions('Audit the change against the task. List every deficit that remains. Record lessons worth keeping.')
  .input({ task: z.string(), summary: z.string() })
  .output({ deficits: z.array(z.string()) });

  .output({ features: z.array(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() })) });

const builder = H.agent('builder', builderRole)
  .model(builderModel)
  .pool(claudePool)
  .recalls([experience, taste])
  .leaseWrites()
  .mustPass(projectChecks);

const auditor = H.agent('auditor', auditorRole)
  .model(sonnet)
  .pool(claudePool)
  .recalls([experience])
  .records(experience);

const planner = H.agent('planner', plannerRole)

const ticketFlow = H.flow('build-and-audit')
  .requires({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() })
  .params({ rounds: z.number() })
  .loop(
    'rounds',
    { carry: { deficits: z.array(z.string()) }, rounds: c => c.params.rounds },
    round => round
      .step('build', builder, c => ({
        task: `${c.input.title}\n\n${c.input.description}`,
        deficits: c.carry ? c.carry.deficits : [],
      }))
      .step('audit', auditor, c => ({
        task: `${c.input.title}\n\n${c.input.description}`,
        summary: c.out.build.summary,
      })),
    last => last.audit.deficits.length === 0 ? null : { deficits: last.audit.deficits },

  .ends(['done', 'unfinished'], c => c.out.rounds.exhausted ? 'unfinished' : 'done');

  .step('plan', planner, c => ({ title: c.input.title, description: c.input.description }))

const heartbeatLane = H.lane('heartbeats', Heartbeat)

  .handler(heartbeatFlow, {

    },
    fields: {

  H.ops.readTelemetry,
  H.ops.readAccounts,

    ticketId: ticket.id,
    category: 'unclassified',
    slaDueAt: ticket.slaDueAt ?? ticket.updatedAt + 14_400_000,

        when: (g) => {

  .requires({ ticketId: z.number(), reason: z.string() })
  .halt('resolution', handlingDecision, { ask: (c) => `Ticket ${c.input.ticketId} escalated: ${c.input.reason}` })

  .clients([claudeCode.supervisor('reviewer', reviewerAccess, { port: H.slot.port(0) })])

# harness-dsl: quota partition, honest attempts, recorded reads (child of g02-minimal-al-0-2-0)

The operator is **scenario-fix**. The worst-handled scenario was **07 (two projects, shared subscriptions)**. The parent's version had four problems:

- It wrote a reduced coding harness rather than scenario 1.
- It had no shared module.
- Its shared quota was an untyped path string that each harness repeated.
- It left the API fallback orphaned outside any pool.

This child gives shared account state an owning entity. It also repairs the adversary's three sharpest critiques: replay determinism, attempt outcomes that lie, and memory scope written as strings.

## Entities

| Sort | Entity | Builder | Produces / is |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kind | **state** | `H.state(name, position)` or `H.state(name, 'terminal', verdict)` | A named, shareable lifecycle position. |
| Kind | **kind** | `H.kind(n).data(z).states(initial, ...others).failsTo(first, ...others?)` | A data shape, its states, and its declared failure moves. |
| Kind | **role** | `H.role(n).input(z).output(z).prompt(f).intents([...])` | What a model call is asked to do. |
| Kind | **memory** | `H.memory(n, 'experience' \| 'taste')` | A memory kind. |
| Kind | **halt** | `H.halt(n, decisionSchema)` | A named outside decision with a typed answer. |
| Kind | **tag** | `H.tag(n)` | A named dimension, such as category, section, model, database or area. |
| Instance | **account** | `cc.subscription(n, { token, quota? })`, `anthropic.account(n, { apiKey, quota? })` | A credential, plus where its quota events live. |
| Instance | **quota ledger** | `sqlite.quota(name, path)` | The quota partition of the ledger: append-only usage, cooldown and cap events. |
| Instance | model, runner, store, memory store, supplier, ledger, guard, observer, client | adapters | Specific resources. |
| Pivot | **agent** | `H.agent(n, role).model(m \| policy)` | role × model. |
| Pivot | **lane** | `H.lane(n, kind).handler(flow, params?)...` | kind × suppliers × store × handler. |
| Pivot | **archive** | `H.archive(n, memory, store)` | memory kind × store: where items live. |
| Pivot | **briefing** | `H.briefing(n, archives, ranking?)` | archives × recall policy: what a call is told. |
| Pivot | **pool** | `H.pool(n, members, policy?)` | accounts × shares × policy, for one harness. |
| Pivot | **trigger** | `H.trigger(n, source, effect)` | A recorded consequence of recorded state. |
| Composite | flow, command, policy, operation | as in the parent | |
| Root | **harness** | `H.harness(n)...start()` | |
| Adapter value | **supervisor session** | `cc.session(n, { endpoints })` | One Claude Code session that can address several control endpoints. |

## Execution vocabulary

- **Run**: one lifetime of a harness process.
- **Attempt**: one execution of one flow phase for one unit.
  - Its states are `running`, `blocked` and `ended`.
  - When ended, its outcome is `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
- **Invocation**: one call of an executable.
- **Recorded call**: any other sequenced `ctx` call. These are `now`, `tag`, `decide`, `children`, `move`, `update`, `remember` and `spawn`. Each is a `recorded` ledger entry.
- **Phase**: the flow body selected by the unit's state at attempt start.

"Step" is not a word in this design.

## Rules

### 1. Skeleton and honest attempt outcomes (principle 12; critique 2)

| The phase returns | Attempt outcome | What happens to the unit |
|---|---|---|
| A state | `succeeded` | Moves to that state. |
| `ctx.wait(state, wake)` | `succeeded` | Parks in a waiting state. |
| `ctx.fail(reason)`, or it throws | `failed` | Stays at its pending state under the lane's retry policy. The default is backoff: 1 minute, doubling, capped at 1 hour. |
| `ctx.fail(reason, to)` | `failed` | Moves to `to`. |
| Interrupted by a move, preemption or cost ceiling | `cancelled` | Handled by the rule that interrupted it. |

**Declared failure moves.**

- `ctx.fail(reason, to)` is allowed only when `to` is among the states the kind declares in `.failsTo(...)`. This is principle 12 as written: a kind declares the move, and only then does a failure move the unit.
- An undeclared `to` is a kernel error. The attempt still fails and the unit does not move.
- A retry policy's `'stop'` moves the unit to the first `failsTo` state.
- `start()` refuses a lane that has `.retry()` when its kind declares no `failsTo`.

**Measurements and reviews do succeed.**

- An hourly Experiment measurement that recorded its sample is an attempt that did what it set out to do. The same holds for a Tenancy review that produced a decision.
- The unit's own outcome is a separate fact: its terminal verdict. Principle 18 forbids conflating the two, and they are not conflated.

### 2. Replay is deterministic by construction (critique 1)

Every `ctx` method that reads from outside the body or writes harness state is sequenced on the ledger. On restart, the phase body re-executes and each sequenced call returns its recorded value.

**Divergence check.**

- Before a sequenced call is accepted, the kernel compares it with the recorded entry at that `seq`: same call type, same executable or halt, same input hash.
- On a mismatch the kernel raises the kernel halt `definition-changed`, with reason `diverged at seq n`. The supervisor resolves it with `restart` or `abandon`.

### 3. Memory scope by reference (critique 3)

- `MemoryDraft.when` is `{ kinds?, roles?, tags? }`, filled with entity references and `TagMatch`.
- Resources and skills are tag dimensions.
- `MemoryItem.when` is stored as a `ScopeRecord` of names.

### 4. Shared account quota (scenario 7; principle 15)

**Where quota lives.**

- Quota is a ledger partition: a `QuotaLedger` of append-only `usage`, `cooldown` and `cap` events, folded at read time.
- Every `Ledger` has a default partition, `ledger.quota`. An account may carry its own partition instead.
- A harness appends its consumption to the account's partition and folds from it. Its single-writer lease never touches the partition.

**Registration.** At start, each harness calls `partition.register(harnessName, ledgerName)` and appends a `cap` event for each pool member's share.

**What each supervisor sees.** `AccountView.byHarness` shows every harness's cap and usage.

### 4a. Keys, grouped firings and deadlines (stated in generation 3)

These rules were implicit in the parent. The scenarios depend on them, so they are now written down.

**Unit keys.**

- A unit has a kernel id and an optional key.
- `create(lane, data, key)` with a key that names a non-terminal unit in that lane is a no-op, and is recorded as such on the firing.
- A key whose unit is terminal names a new unit. The old unit keeps its id and its history.
- `move(lane, key, state)` targets the non-terminal unit with that key, and is a no-op when there is none.
- Supplies with `create` follow the same rule. A webhook and a poll that both deliver one conversation therefore produce one unit.

**Grouped firings.**

- A metric source grouped by a tag records its firing with `tags[group.name] = group`.
- Units that the firing's effects create inherit that tag from their first transition onward.
- As a result, "audits opened per category" is a `countBy` over transitions, with no extra bookkeeping.

**Deadlines.**

- A `deadline` source re-reads `due(data)` after every recorded change to the unit's data. This covers flow `update`, supply `patch` and the control API's `work.update`.
- Re-reading disarms the old timer, so a deadline that was moved never fires at its old time.
- Arming and re-arming are `recorded` entries, so the timer is ledger state.

### 5. Recall, supply, triggers, scheduler, cost, durability, control, validation

These are as in the parent, with the changes above. Startup validation additionally refuses:

- a `failsTo` state that is not one of the kind's states;
- a quota partition registered by a different ledger under the same harness name.

## What changed and why

**Generation 2 (versus the parent).**

- Scenario 7: added `QuotaLedger`, `sqlite.quota`, `Account.quota`, `QuotaEvent` with `cap`, `AccountView.byHarness`, `Endpoint`, `http.control().endpoint` and `cc.session`.
- Critique 1: `ctx.now()` and `ctx.tag()` became async recorded calls, and the divergence check was added.
- Critique 2: added `failsTo` and `ctx.fail(reason, to)`.
- Critique 3: `Scope` now takes entity references and `TagMatch`. `ctx.children` is typed, and `Metrics.sum` returns `Total`.

**Generation 3 (writing scenarios 06 to 10 against this surface).**

- **Added `Metrics.countBy({ among, by, ...window })`.**
  - Scenario 9 asks for "how many Audits were opened per category this month". `rateBy` could only answer it by passing one filter twice and reading `samples`, which is a counting question disguised as a rate.
  - `countBy` returns `Total` per tag value. It is the one new method, and scenario 9 calls it.
- **Stated §4a.** These are not new surface. Scenarios 6, 8, 9 and 10 depend on three semantics the parent left implicit:
  - Scenario 9's Audit deduplication and the webhook-plus-poll supply in scenarios 2 and 9 depend on key reuse.
  - Scenario 9's per-category audit count depends on the grouped-firing tag.
  - Scenario 9's SLA extension through the supervisor depends on deadline re-arming. The old deadline never fires.
- **Scenario 7** is written as one exported `shared` object and two functions, `codingTeam(shared)` and `documentation(shared)`. The coding harness is all of scenario 1. The owner's session addresses both `http.control` endpoints.
- **Scenario 8 keeps the skeleton.**
  - Experiment: `aWins` and `bWins` are success, `inconclusive` is neutral.
  - Tenancy: waits between monthly reviews in a waiting state, is suspended into another waiting state, and churns into a neutral terminal state.
  - Negotiation: each round is one attempt that ends in `ctx.wait`. The vendor webhook supplies `update` and never creates a unit. Expiry is a deadline trigger.
  - Success rate therefore keeps its meaning: success over success plus failure verdicts, with neutral counted beside them.

## Principles broken

None.

- **Principle 14.** The envelope's skills and resources are carried as typed tag matches. Every dimension the principle names is still in `when`.
- **Principle 15.** Shared quota is an append-only partition of the ledger, carried by the account instance. It takes no lock and does not share the ledger's name.

import { z } from 'zod';

const queued = H.state('queued', 'pending');
const building = H.state('building', 'active');
const done = H.state('done', 'terminal', 'success');
const wontfix = H.state('wontfix', 'terminal', 'neutral');
const planning = H.state('planning', 'active');
const featuresInFlight = H.state('featuresInFlight', 'waiting');
const assembling = H.state('assembling', 'pending');
const due = H.state('due', 'pending');
const probing = H.state('probing', 'active');
const healthy = H.state('healthy', 'terminal', 'success');
const down = H.state('down', 'terminal', 'failure');

const ticket = z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() });

const Bug = H.kind('Bug').data(ticket).states(queued, building, done, wontfix);
const Feature = H.kind('Feature')
  .data(ticket.extend({ epic: z.string().optional() }))
  .states(queued, building, done, wontfix);
const Epic = H.kind('Epic').data(ticket).states(queued, planning, featuresInFlight, assembling, done, wontfix);
const Heartbeat = H.kind('Heartbeat').data(z.object({ service: z.string() })).states(due, probing, healthy, down);

const builderRole = H.role('builder')
  .input(z.object({
    title: z.string(),
    description: z.string(),
    deficits: z.array(z.string()),
    decision: z.string().optional(),
  }))
  .output(z.object({ summary: z.string(), question: z.string().optional() }))
  .prompt((input) =>
    `Implement: ${input.title}\n\n${input.description}\n\nOpen deficits:\n${input.deficits.join('\n')}\n\nOwner decision: ${input.decision ?? 'none'}`)
  .intents(['read', 'edit', 'execute']);

const auditorRole = H.role('auditor')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string(), summary: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ deficits: z.array(z.string()) }))
  .prompt((input) => `Audit the change for "${input.title}".\n\n${input.description}\n\nBuilder summary: ${input.summary}`)
  .intents(['read', 'execute']);

const plannerRole = H.role('planner')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ features: z.array(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() })) }))
  .prompt((input) => `Decompose the epic "${input.title}" into features.\n\n${input.description}`)
  .intents(['read']);

const experience = H.memory('experience', 'experience');
const taste = H.memory('taste', 'taste');
const teamExperience = H.archive('team-experience', experience, jsonl.memory('.harness/experience.jsonl'));
const ownerTaste = H.archive('owner-taste', taste, jsonl.memory('.harness/taste.jsonl'));
const buildBriefing = H.briefing('build-briefing', [teamExperience, ownerTaste]);
const auditBriefing = H.briefing('audit-briefing', [teamExperience]);
const planBriefing = H.briefing('plan-briefing', [ownerTaste]);

const sonnet = cc.model('claude-sonnet-4-5');
const opus = cc.model('claude-opus-4-1');

const cheapUntilWeak = H.policy.model('cheap-until-weak', (choice) => {
  const record = choice.metrics.successRate({ kind: choice.kind, model: sonnet, days: 14 });
  if (record.samples < 20 || record.value === null) return sonnet;
  return record.value < 0.85 ? opus : sonnet;
});

const subscriptionOne = cc.subscription('claude-1', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_TOKEN_1') });
const subscriptionTwo = cc.subscription('claude-2', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_TOKEN_2') });
const subscriptionThree = cc.subscription('claude-3', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_TOKEN_3') });
const apiFallback = anthropic.account('api-fallback', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') });

const soonestExpiringFirst = H.policy.account('soonest-expiring-first', (choice) => {
  const open = choice.accounts.filter(
    (view) => view.eligible && view.account.plan === 'subscription' && view.usedShare < view.share
  );
  const ordered = [...open].sort(
    (a, b) => (a.windowEndsAt?.getTime() ?? Infinity) - (b.windowEndsAt?.getTime() ?? Infinity)
  );
  const first = ordered[0];
  if (first) return first.account;
  const metered = choice.accounts.find((view) => view.eligible && view.account.plan === 'metered');
  return metered ? metered.account : null;
});

const claudePool = H.pool(
  'claude',
  [
    { account: subscriptionOne, share: 0.7 },
    { account: subscriptionTwo, share: 0.7 },
    { account: subscriptionThree, share: 0.5 },
    { account: apiFallback, share: 1 },
  ],
  soonestExpiringFirst
);

const worktrees = git.worktree('worktrees', { repo: '.', slots: 3 });
const local = shell.local('local', { slots: 4 });

const projectChecks = H.command('project-checks').argv(() => ['npm', 'run', 'check']);

const builder = H.agent('builder', builderRole)
  .model(cheapUntilWeak)
  .on(worktrees)
  .recalls(buildBriefing)
  .guards(cc.fileLeases(), cc.stopCheck(projectChecks));

const auditor = H.agent('auditor', auditorRole)
  .model(opus)
  .on(worktrees)
  .recalls(auditBriefing)
  .records(teamExperience);

const planner = H.agent('planner', plannerRole).model(opus).recalls(planBriefing);

const ownerDecision = H.halt('owner-decision', z.object({ decision: z.string() }));

const buildAndAudit = H.flow('build-and-audit')
  .for(Bug, Feature)
  .params(z.object({ rounds: z.number().int().positive() }))
  .does(async (ctx) => {
    await ctx.move('building');
    const { title, description } = ctx.unit.data;
    let deficits: string[] = [];
    let decision: string | undefined;
    for (let round = 1; round <= ctx.params.rounds; round += 1) {
      const built = await ctx.run(builder, { title, description, deficits, decision });
      if (!built.ok) return ctx.fail(built.error);
      if (built.value.question) {
        const answer = await ctx.halt(ownerDecision, built.value.question);
        decision = answer.decision;
        continue;
      }
      const audit = await ctx.run(auditor, { title, description, summary: built.value.summary });
      if (!audit.ok) return ctx.fail(audit.error);
      if (audit.value.deficits.length === 0) return 'done';
      deficits = audit.value.deficits;
    }
    return ctx.fail(`deficits remain after ${ctx.params.rounds} rounds`);
  });

const linearKey = H.env('LINEAR_API_KEY');

const bugTracker = linear.tracker(Bug, {
  apiKey: linearKey,
  team: 'PRODUCT',
  label: 'bug',
  read: (issue) => ({ title: issue.title, description: issue.description }),
  statuses: { queued: 'Todo', building: 'In Progress', done: 'Done', wontfix: 'Canceled' },
});

const featureTracker = linear.tracker(Feature, {
  apiKey: linearKey,
  team: 'PRODUCT',
  label: 'feature',
  read: (issue) => ({ title: issue.title, description: issue.description, epic: issue.parentId }),
  statuses: { queued: 'Todo', building: 'In Progress', done: 'Done', wontfix: 'Canceled' },
});

const epicTracker = linear.tracker(Epic, {
  apiKey: linearKey,
  team: 'PRODUCT',
  label: 'epic',
  read: (issue) => ({ title: issue.title, description: issue.description }),
  statuses: {
    queued: 'Todo',
    planning: 'Planning',
    featuresInFlight: 'In Progress',
    assembling: 'In Review',
    done: 'Done',
    wontfix: 'Canceled',
  },
});

const bugFolder = folder.files(Bug, {
  dir: 'bugs',
  read: (file) => ({ title: String(file.frontmatter['title'] ?? file.path), description: file.body }),
});

const bugs = H.lane('bugs', Bug)
  .handler(buildAndAudit, { rounds: 3 })
  .suppliers(bugTracker, bugFolder, H.operator)
  .store(bugTracker)
  .wip(2);

const features = H.lane('features', Feature)
  .handler(buildAndAudit, { rounds: 5 })
  .suppliers(featureTracker, H.operator)
  .store(featureTracker);

const epicFlow = H.flow('epic')
  .for(Epic)
  .does(async (ctx) => {
    await ctx.move('planning');
    const plan = await ctx.run(planner, { title: ctx.unit.data.title, description: ctx.unit.data.description });
    if (!plan.ok) return ctx.fail(plan.error);
    await ctx.spawn(features, plan.value.features.map((feature) => ({ ...feature, epic: ctx.unit.key })));
    return ctx.wait('featuresInFlight', { children: true, then: 'assembling' });
  })
  .phase('assembling', async (ctx) => {
    const children = await ctx.children(features);
    if (children.some((child) => child.position !== 'terminal')) {
      return ctx.wait('featuresInFlight', { children: true, then: 'assembling' });
    }
    return 'done';
  });

const epics = H.lane('epics', Epic).handler(epicFlow).suppliers(epicTracker).store(epicTracker).wip(1);

const probe = H.command('service-probe')
  .input(z.object({ service: z.string() }))
  .argv((input) => ['curl', '-fsS', `https://${input.service}.internal/health`])
  .on(local);

const heartbeatFlow = H.flow('heartbeat')
  .for(Heartbeat)
  .does(async (ctx) => {
    await ctx.move('probing');
    const result = await ctx.run(probe, { service: ctx.unit.data.service });
    return result.ok ? 'healthy' : 'down';
  });

const heartbeatClock = H.clock('every-five-minutes', Heartbeat, { every: { minutes: 5 } }, () => [
  { create: { service: 'api' } },
]);

const heartbeats = H.lane('heartbeats', Heartbeat).handler(heartbeatFlow).suppliers(heartbeatClock);

const outageFilesBug = H.trigger('outage-files-bug', H.on.enters(Heartbeat, 'down'), (event, act) =>
  act.create(bugs, {
    title: `Heartbeat down: ${event.unit.data.service}`,
    description: `The ${event.unit.data.service} heartbeat failed at ${event.at.toISOString()}.`,
  })
);

const laneOrder = [heartbeats.name, bugs.name, features.name, epics.name];
const starvedAfterMs = 2 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
const rank = (unit: PendingView): number =>
  unit.lane === features.name && unit.waitedMs > starvedAfterMs ? 0.5 : laneOrder.indexOf(unit.lane);

const scheduler = H.policy.scheduler('heartbeats-bugs-features-epics', (view) => ({
  start: [...view.pending].sort((a, b) => rank(a) - rank(b) || b.waitedMs - a.waitedMs),
}));

const productionHealth = H.command('production-health')
  .argv(() => ['curl', '-fsS', 'https://status.example.com/health'])
  .on(local);

const supervisor = cc.supervisor({
  grants: [
    H.ops.readWork,
    H.ops.writeWork,
    H.ops.resolveHalts,
    H.ops.writeMemory,
    H.ops.readTelemetry,
    H.ops.readAccounts,
    H.ops.setShares,
    H.operation('production-health', productionHealth),
  ],
});

export const codingTeam = H.harness('coding-team')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('.harness/ledger.db'))
  .lanes(heartbeats, bugs, features, epics)
  .pools(claudePool)
  .triggers(outageFilesBug)
  .scheduler(scheduler)
  .clients(supervisor)
  .observers(markdown.board('BOARD.md'), markdown.telemetry('TELEMETRY.md'));

export const running = codingTeam.start();

  readonly b: readonly number[];
}

const experimentVerdict = H.policy.rule('experiment-verdict', (samples: Samples, metrics: Metrics): ExperimentResult => {
  const history = metrics.rate({
    among: { entry: 'transition', kind: Experiment, position: 'terminal' },
    count: { entry: 'transition', kind: Experiment, state: inconclusive },
    days: 365,
  });
  const oftenInconclusive = history.samples >= 10 && history.value !== null && history.value > 0.5;
  const margin = oftenInconclusive ? 0.02 : 0.05;
  const a = mean(samples.a);
  const b = mean(samples.b);
  const baseline = Math.max(Math.abs(a), Math.abs(b), 1e-9);
  if ((a - b) / baseline > margin) return 'a';
  if ((b - a) / baseline > margin) return 'b';
  return 'inconclusive';
});

const measure = H.command('measure-experiment')
  .input(z.object({ name: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ a: z.number(), b: z.number() }))
  .argv(e => ['experiment-metric', '--experiment', e.name, '--json'])
  .on(local)
  .recovers('rerun');

const experimentFlow = H.flow('hourly-measurement').for(Experiment).does(async ctx => {
  await ctx.move('measuring');
  const now = await ctx.now();
  const experiment = ctx.unit.data;
  const startedAt = experiment.startedAt ?? now.toISOString();
  const sample = await ctx.run(measure, { name: experiment.name });
  if (!sample.ok) return ctx.fail(sample.error);
  const samplesA = [...experiment.samplesA, sample.value.a];
  const samplesB = [...experiment.samplesB, sample.value.b];
  await ctx.update({ startedAt, samplesA, samplesB });
  if (now.getTime() - Date.parse(startedAt) < twoWeeksMs) {
    return ctx.wait('collecting', { at: new Date(now.getTime() + hourMs), then: 'scheduled' });
  }
  const result = await ctx.decide(experimentVerdict, { a: samplesA, b: samplesB });
  return result === 'a' ? 'a-wins' : result === 'b' ? 'b-wins' : 'inconclusive';
});

const reviewDue = H.state('review-due', 'pending');
const reviewing = H.state('reviewing', 'active');
const between = H.state('between-reviews', 'waiting');
const suspended = H.state('suspended', 'waiting');
const churned = H.state('churned', 'terminal', 'neutral');

const Tenancy = H.kind('tenancy')
  .data(z.object({ tenant: z.string(), lastReview: z.string().optional(), upsold: z.boolean().optional() }))
  .states(reviewDue, reviewing, between, suspended, churned);

const usageReport = H.command('usage-report')
  .input(z.object({ tenant: z.string() }))
  .argv(t => ['usage-report', '--tenant', t.tenant, '--last-month'])
  .on(local)
  .recovers('rerun');

const tenancySummaryRole = H.role('tenancy-summarizer')
  .input(z.object({ tenant: z.string(), usage: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ summary: z.string(), upsellCase: z.string() }))
  .prompt(t => `Summarise last month's usage for ${t.tenant} and state the case for or against an upsell:\n${t.usage}`);
const tenancySummarizer = H.agent('tenancy-summarizer', tenancySummaryRole).model(strong);

const upsellDecision = H.halt('upsell-decision', z.object({ upsell: z.boolean(), note: z.string() }));

const tenancyFlow = H.flow('monthly-tenancy-review').for(Tenancy).does(async ctx => {
  await ctx.move('reviewing');
  const tenancy = ctx.unit.data;
  const usage = await ctx.run(usageReport, { tenant: tenancy.tenant });
  if (!usage.ok) return ctx.fail(usage.error);
  const summary = await ctx.run(tenancySummarizer, { tenant: tenancy.tenant, usage: usage.value });
  if (!summary.ok) return ctx.fail(summary.error);
  const decision = await ctx.halt(upsellDecision, `${summary.value.summary}\n\n${summary.value.upsellCase}`);
  const now = await ctx.now();
  await ctx.update({ lastReview: now.toISOString(), upsold: decision.upsell });
  return ctx.wait('between-reviews', { at: firstOfNextMonth(now), then: 'review-due' });
});

const billingEvents = http.webhook(Tenancy, {
  path: '/billing',
  secret: H.env('BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET'),
  body: z.object({ tenant: z.string(), event: z.enum(['signed', 'suspended', 'reinstated', 'churned']) }),
  read: b =>
    b.event === 'signed'
      ? { create: { tenant: b.tenant }, key: b.tenant }
      : {
          update: b.tenant,
          state: b.event === 'suspended' ? 'suspended' : b.event === 'reinstated' ? 'review-due' : 'churned',
        },
});

const ourTurn = H.state('our-turn', 'pending');
const drafting = H.state('drafting', 'active');
const theirTurn = H.state('their-turn', 'waiting');
const agreed = H.state('agreed', 'terminal', 'success');
const walkedAwayUs = H.state('walked-away-by-us', 'terminal', 'neutral');
const walkedAwayThem = H.state('walked-away-by-them', 'terminal', 'failure');
const expired = H.state('expired', 'terminal', 'failure');

const negotiationData = z.object({
  vendor: z.string(),
  item: z.string(),
  expiresAt: z.string(),
  lastReply: z.string().optional(),
  history: z.array(z.object({ from: z.enum(['us', 'them']), text: z.string() })),
});
type NegotiationData = z.infer<typeof negotiationData>;

const Negotiation = H.kind('negotiation')
  .data(negotiationData)
  .states(ourTurn, drafting, theirTurn, agreed, walkedAwayUs, walkedAwayThem, expired);

const negotiatorRole = H.role('negotiator')
  .input(z.object({ vendor: z.string(), item: z.string(), history: z.array(z.object({ from: z.string(), text: z.string() })) }))
  .output(z.object({ offer: z.string(), walkAway: z.boolean() }))
  .prompt(n => `Draft our next offer to ${n.vendor} for ${n.item}, or walk away.\n${n.history.map(h => `${h.from}: ${h.text}`).join('\n')}`);
const negotiator = H.agent('negotiator', negotiatorRole).model(strong);

const sendOffer = H.command('send-offer')
  .input(z.object({ negotiation: z.string(), vendor: z.string(), offer: z.string() }))
  .argv(o => ['send-offer', '--negotiation', o.negotiation, '--vendor', o.vendor, '--text', o.offer])
  .on(local)
  .recovers('park');

const negotiationFlow = H.flow('negotiation-round').for(Negotiation).does(async ctx => {
  await ctx.move('drafting');
  const negotiation = ctx.unit.data;
  const history: NegotiationData['history'] = negotiation.lastReply
    ? [...negotiation.history, { from: 'them', text: negotiation.lastReply }]
    : negotiation.history;
  const next = await ctx.run(negotiator, { vendor: negotiation.vendor, item: negotiation.item, history });
  if (!next.ok) return ctx.fail(next.error);
  if (next.value.walkAway) {
    await ctx.update({ history, lastReply: undefined });
    return 'walked-away-by-us';
  }
  const sent = await ctx.run(sendOffer, { negotiation: ctx.unit.key, vendor: negotiation.vendor, offer: next.value.offer });
  if (!sent.ok) return ctx.fail(sent.error);
  const withOffer: NegotiationData['history'] = [...history, { from: 'us', text: next.value.offer }];
  await ctx.update({ history: withOffer, lastReply: undefined });
  return ctx.wait('their-turn', { then: 'our-turn' });
});

const vendorReplies = http.webhook(Negotiation, {
  path: '/vendor-replies',
  secret: H.env('VENDOR_WEBHOOK_SECRET'),
  body: z.object({ negotiation: z.string(), type: z.enum(['reply', 'accept', 'walk-away']), text: z.string() }),
  read: b =>
    b.type === 'reply'
      ? { update: b.negotiation, patch: { lastReply: b.text }, state: 'our-turn' }
      : { update: b.negotiation, state: b.type === 'accept' ? 'agreed' : 'walked-away-by-them' },
});

const negotiationExpires = H.trigger(
  'negotiation-expires',
  H.on.deadline(Negotiation, n => new Date(n.expiresAt), ['our-turn', 'drafting', 'their-turn']),
  (_event, act) => act.move('expired')
);

const experiments = H.lane('experiments', Experiment).handler(experimentFlow).suppliers(H.operator).store(sqlite.store(Experiment, './.harness/units.sqlite'));
const tenancies = H.lane('tenancies', Tenancy).handler(tenancyFlow).suppliers(H.operator, billingEvents).store(sqlite.store(Tenancy, './.harness/units.sqlite'));
const negotiations = H.lane('negotiations', Negotiation).handler(negotiationFlow).suppliers(H.operator, vendorReplies).store(sqlite.store(Negotiation, './.harness/units.sqlite'));

const pool = H.pool('anthropic', [{ account: anthropic.account('business', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') }), share: 1 }]);

export const harness = H.harness('business-lifecycles')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('./.harness/ledger.sqlite'))
  .lanes(experiments, tenancies, negotiations)
  .pools(pool)
  .triggers(negotiationExpires)
  .scheduler(H.policy.scheduler('oldest-first', view => ({ start: [...view.pending].sort((x, y) => y.waitedMs - x.waitedMs) })))
  .clients(cc.supervisor({ grants: [H.ops.readWork, H.ops.writeWork, H.ops.resolveHalts, H.ops.readTelemetry] }))
  .observers(markdown.board('./BOARD.md'), markdown.telemetry('./TELEMETRY.md'));

export const running = harness.start();

=== END ===

=== FILE: scenarios/09-self-watch.ts ===
import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import type { Metrics, PendingView } from 'harness-dsl';
import * as anthropic from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import * as cc from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import * as http from 'harness-dsl/http';
import * as sqlite from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import * as jsonl from 'harness-dsl/jsonl';
import * as shell from 'harness-dsl/shell';
import * as markdown from 'harness-dsl/markdown';
import { z } from 'zod';

const category = H.tag('category');

const fresh = H.state('new', 'pending');
const classifying = H.state('classifying', 'pending');
const drafting = H.state('drafting', 'active');
const awaitingApproval = H.state('awaiting-approval', 'active');
const sent = H.state('sent', 'waiting');
const closedByCustomer = H.state('closed-by-customer', 'terminal', 'success');
const escalated = H.state('escalated', 'terminal', 'failure');

const Conversation = H.kind('conversation')
  .data(z.object({ customer: z.string(), latest: z.string(), category: z.string().optional(), slaDueAt: z.string() }))
  .states(fresh, classifying, drafting, awaitingApproval, sent, closedByCustomer, escalated)
  .failsTo('escalated', 'classifying');

const queued = H.state('queued', 'pending');
const handling = H.state('handling', 'active');
const resolved = H.state('resolved', 'terminal', 'success');

const Escalation = H.kind('escalation')
  .data(z.object({ conversation: z.string(), reason: z.string() }))
  .states(queued, handling, resolved);

const auditOpen = H.state('audit-open', 'pending');
const auditing = H.state('auditing', 'active');
const auditClosed = H.state('audit-closed', 'terminal', 'success');
const auditWithdrawn = H.state('audit-withdrawn', 'terminal', 'neutral');

const Audit = H.kind('audit')
  .data(z.object({ category: z.string(), rate: z.number() }))
  .states(auditOpen, auditing, auditClosed, auditWithdrawn);

const taste = H.archive('support-taste', H.memory('support-taste', 'taste'), jsonl.memory('./.harness/taste.jsonl'));
const experience = H.archive('support-experience', H.memory('support-experience', 'experience'), jsonl.memory('./.harness/experience.jsonl'));
const drafterBriefing = H.briefing('drafter-briefing', [taste, experience]);

const classifierRole = H.role('classifier')
  .input(z.object({ message: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ category: z.string() }))
  .prompt(m => `Classify this customer message into one support category:\n${m.message}`);
const drafterRole = H.role('drafter')
  .input(z.object({ customer: z.string(), category: z.string(), message: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ reply: z.string() }))
  .prompt(m => `Draft a reply to ${m.customer} about a ${m.category} issue:\n${m.message}`);

const classifier = H.agent('classifier', classifierRole).model(anthropic.model('claude-haiku-4-5'));
const drafter = H.agent('drafter', drafterRole).model(anthropic.model('claude-sonnet-4-5')).recalls(drafterBriefing);

const approval = H.halt('reply-approval', z.object({
  approved: z.boolean(),
  editedReply: z.string().optional(),
  tasteNote: z.string().optional(),
}));
const escalationResolution = H.halt('escalation-resolution', z.object({ note: z.string() }));
const auditFinding = H.halt('audit-finding', z.object({ finding: z.string() }));

const safeCategory = H.policy.rule('safe-category', (name: string, metrics: Metrics): boolean => {
  const scope = [category.is(name)];
  const record = metrics.rate({
    among: { ...approval.resolved(), tags: scope },
    count: { ...approval.resolved({ approved: true }), tags: scope },
    days: 3650,
  });
  return record.samples >= 200 && record.hits === record.samples;
});

const local = shell.local('local', { slots: 4 });
const helpdeskHeaders = { authorization: H.env('HELPDESK_TOKEN') };

const sendReply = H.command('send-reply')
  .input(z.object({ conversation: z.string(), text: z.string() }))
  .argv(r => ['helpdesk-reply', '--conversation', r.conversation, '--text', r.text])
  .on(local)
  .recovers('park');

const conversationFlow = H.flow('triage-and-reply').for(Conversation).does(async ctx => {
  const conversation = ctx.unit.data;
  const classified = await ctx.run(classifier, { message: conversation.latest });
  if (!classified.ok) return ctx.fail(classified.error);
  const cat = classified.value.category;
  await ctx.update({ category: cat });
  await ctx.tag(category, cat);

  await ctx.move('drafting');
  const draft = await ctx.run(
    drafter,
    { customer: conversation.customer, category: cat, message: conversation.latest },
    { scope: { tags: [category.is(cat)] } }
  );
  if (!draft.ok) return ctx.fail(draft.error);

  let reply = draft.value.reply;
  const safe = await ctx.decide(safeCategory, cat);
  if (!safe) {
    await ctx.move('awaiting-approval');
    const decision = await ctx.halt(approval, reply);
    if (decision.tasteNote) {
      await ctx.remember(taste, { text: decision.tasteNote, when: { roles: [drafterRole] }, status: 'candidate' });
    }
    if (!decision.approved) return ctx.fail('reply rejected by reviewer', 'classifying');
    reply = decision.editedReply ?? reply;
  }

  const posted = await ctx.run(sendReply, { conversation: ctx.unit.key, text: reply });
  if (!posted.ok) return ctx.fail(posted.error);
  return 'sent';
});

const escalationFlow = H.flow('human-escalation').for(Escalation).does(async ctx => {
  await ctx.move('handling');
  await ctx.halt(escalationResolution, `Conversation ${ctx.unit.data.conversation}: ${ctx.unit.data.reason}`);
  return 'resolved';
});

interface ReportInput {
  readonly category: string;
  readonly since: Date;
}

const selfWatchReport = H.policy.rule('self-watch-report', (input: ReportInput, metrics: Metrics): string => {
  const opened = metrics.countBy({ among: { entry: 'transition', kind: Audit, state: auditOpen }, by: category, since: input.since });
  const paused = metrics.sum({ of: 'durationMs', among: { entry: 'lane', lane: conversations, status: 'resumed' }, since: input.since });
  const thisCategory = opened[input.category]?.value ?? 0;
  return `${thisCategory} audits opened for ${input.category} this month; conversations lane paused ${Math.round(paused.value / 60000)} minutes over ${paused.samples} pauses.`;
});

function monthStart(now: Date): Date {
  return new Date(Date.UTC(now.getUTCFullYear(), now.getUTCMonth(), 1));
}

const auditFlow = H.flow('human-audit').for(Audit).does(async ctx => {
  await ctx.move('auditing');
  const audit = ctx.unit.data;
  const report = await ctx.decide(selfWatchReport, { category: audit.category, since: monthStart(await ctx.now()) });
  await ctx.halt(auditFinding, `Approval rate for ${audit.category} fell to ${audit.rate.toFixed(2)}. ${report}`);
  return 'audit-closed';
});

const helpdeskEvents = http.webhook(Conversation, {
  path: '/helpdesk',
  secret: H.env('HELPDESK_WEBHOOK_SECRET'),
  body: z.object({
    type: z.enum(['created', 'replied', 'closed']),
    id: z.string(),
    customer: z.string(),
    message: z.string(),
    slaDueAt: z.string(),
  }),
  read: b =>
    b.type === 'created'
      ? { create: { customer: b.customer, latest: b.message, slaDueAt: b.slaDueAt }, key: b.id }
      : b.type === 'replied'
        ? { update: b.id, patch: { latest: b.message }, state: 'classifying' }
        : { update: b.id, state: 'closed-by-customer' },
});

const helpdeskPoll = http.poll(Conversation, {
  url: 'https://helpdesk.example.com/api/conversations?status=open',
  every: { minutes: 10 },
  headers: helpdeskHeaders,
  body: z.object({
    conversations: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string(), customer: z.string(), message: z.string(), slaDueAt: z.string() })),
  }),
  read: b => b.conversations.map(c => ({ create: { customer: c.customer, latest: c.message, slaDueAt: c.slaDueAt }, key: c.id })),
});

const conversations = H.lane('conversations', Conversation)
  .handler(conversationFlow)
  .suppliers(helpdeskEvents, helpdeskPoll)
  .store(http.store(Conversation, { url: 'https://helpdesk.example.com/api/conversations', headers: helpdeskHeaders, stateField: 'harness_state' }))
  .maxUsdPerUnit(0.4);
const escalations = H.lane('escalations', Escalation).handler(escalationFlow);
const audits = H.lane('audits', Audit).handler(auditFlow);

const slaBreach = H.trigger(
  'sla-breach-escalates',
  H.on.deadline(Conversation, c => new Date(c.slaDueAt), ['new', 'classifying', 'drafting', 'awaiting-approval']),
  (event, act) => [
    act.move('escalated'),
    act.create(escalations, { conversation: event.unit.key, reason: 'SLA breached' }, `escalation-${event.unit.key}`),
  ]
);

const approvalSlump = H.trigger(
  'approval-slump-opens-audit',
  H.on.metric(
    m => m.rateBy({ among: approval.resolved(), count: approval.resolved({ approved: true }), by: category, days: 7 }),
    { trip: { below: 0.9 }, reset: { above: 0.95 }, minSamples: 50, group: category }
  ),
  (event, act) =>
    event.state === 'tripped'
      ? [
          act.create(audits, { category: event.group, rate: event.rate.value ?? 0 }, `audit-${event.group}`),
          act.remember(experience, {
            text: `when drafting for ${event.group}, recall the stricter phrasing`,
            because: `approvals fell to ${(event.rate.value ?? 0).toFixed(2)} over ${event.rate.samples} samples`,
            when: { roles: [drafterRole], tags: [category.is(event.group)] },
            status: 'candidate',
          }),
        ]
      : act.move(audits, `audit-${event.group}`, 'audit-withdrawn')
);

const modelErrors = H.trigger(
  'model-errors-pause-conversations',
  H.on.metric(
    m => m.rate({
      among: { entry: 'invocation', mode: 'model', status: 'ended' },
      count: { entry: 'invocation', mode: 'model', status: 'ended', ok: false },
      hours: 1,
    }),
    { trip: { above: 0.2 }, reset: { below: 0.05 }, minSamples: 20 }
  ),
  (event, act) => (event.state === 'tripped' ? act.pause(conversations) : act.resume(conversations))
);

const breachAt = (p: PendingView): number => (p.is(Conversation) ? Date.parse(p.data.slaDueAt) : 0);

const timeToBreach = H.policy.scheduler('time-to-breach', view => ({
  start: [...view.pending].sort((x, y) => breachAt(x) - breachAt(y)),
}));

const pool = H.pool('anthropic', [{ account: anthropic.account('support', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') }), share: 1 }]);

const reviewer = cc.supervisor({
  grants: [H.ops.readWork, H.ops.writeWork, H.ops.resolveHalts, H.ops.readMemory, H.ops.writeMemory, H.ops.curateMemory, H.ops.readTelemetry],
});

export const harness = H.harness('support-triage')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('./.harness/ledger.sqlite'))
  .lanes(conversations, escalations, audits)
  .pools(pool)
  .triggers(slaBreach, approvalSlump, modelErrors)
  .scheduler(timeToBreach)
  .clients(reviewer)
  .observers(markdown.board('./BOARD.md'), markdown.telemetry('./TELEMETRY.md'));

export const running = harness.start();

=== END ===

# You are designing harness-dsl, a TypeScript DSL for stateful agentic-work harnesses.

# harness-dsl design principles

These are the owner's decisions. A variant that violates one is worse, however elegant. A variant may propose changing one only by stating the principle it breaks and why, in its design notes.

## Vision

1. **Stateless LLMs, stateful harness.** Every model call is a pure function. All state lives in the harness. The harness gets better over time not because models learn but because it feeds the right memory to the right call.
2. **The harness is about work.** Units of work, kinds of work (Bug, Feature, Epic, ServiceHeartbeat, Exercise), hierarchies of kinds, lifecycles, where work comes from, where its state lives, what runs next. The framework is honest about this. It does not hide behind "general purpose".
3. **An LLM is a component, not a requirement.** A harness with zero model calls is a first-class harness. Deterministic scripts and model calls compose through the same executable interface.
4. **Intelligence lives in determinism.** Policies (what to pick, what to recall, what to schedule) are deterministic functions, authored once, reading harness state and metrics at decision time. Policies never change themselves. The harness changes behaviour because policies read changed state.

## Dividing line

5. **Opinionated about shape, agnostic about backend.** The kernel defines what a work unit, a lifecycle, a memory item, a policy, a ledger entry *is*. It never cares where any of them is stored, which vendor serves a model, or which tool the operator uses. Like Eloquent: strict about how you model, indifferent to which database.
6. **Defaults ship, and pass the delete test.** First-party backends ship in the box (SQLite ledger, JSONL memory store, Claude Code driver, folder supplier). Each is one implementation of a public interface. Delete any of them and the kernel still compiles and runs.
7. **`H.*` is kernel vocabulary only.** Shapes and builders. Anything with a backend lives in a subpath (`harness-dsl/claude-code`, `harness-dsl/sqlite`, `harness-dsl/linear`), whether first-party or not. No vendor, CLI, file format or product name appears in `H.*`.
8. **Three sorts of entity.** *Kinds* are pure vocabulary and carry no backend (work kind, state, memory kind, role). *Instances* are specific resources and carry their backend (account, model, runner). *Pivots* connect kinds and instances per harness (pool = accounts × policy, agent = role × model, lane = work kind × suppliers × store × handler, journal = memory kind × store × recall).
9. **Every pivot has a noun.** A pivot enters the DSL only when we can name what it produces. `bind`, `wire`, `attach`, `connect` are not nouns; they are the absence of a concept.
10. **Relationships do not live on kinds.** A work kind does not know who supplies it, stores it or handles it. A role does not know which model runs it. Putting a relationship on a kind makes the kind less reusable.

## Mechanics

11. **Descriptors are immutable and stateless.** Every builder method returns a new descriptor. Nothing is read from the environment at definition time; `H.env('NAME')` and `H.slot.port(n)` are references the runtime resolves. Derived descriptors must be renamed; the runtime refuses two descriptors with one name.
12. **Lifecycle skeleton.** An attempt has one of three outcomes: succeeded, failed, cancelled. This is the harness's track record, and metrics on models, agents, runners and accounts are computed from it. A unit is at one of four positions: pending, active, waiting (parked, holding no capacity, not schedulable), terminal. The scheduler and the board are defined on positions. A kind's named states are entities (shareable); each declares its position, and each terminal state declares its verdict for the kind's own outcome rate: success, failure or neutral, with no default. Blocked (waiting on a human) is an attempt state, not a unit state. A unit outlives its attempts. By default a failed attempt leaves the unit at pending under the lane's retry policy; a kind may declare a move for a failure, and only then does an attempt's failure move the unit. (Amended 2026-11-01 after generation 0: eight of eight variants broke the five-outcome form, and the adversaries showed why. The failure default was added after generation 1, when three of eleven children read the silence as "every kind declares a failure state" and invented states that loop or dead-end.)
13. **Triggers are relationships.** A trigger connects a source (a transition, later also time, external events, metric thresholds) to a consequence (create work in a lane, run an executable, record memory). Flows stay blind to other kinds. Triggers fire only from recorded ledger events and their firings are recorded.
14. **Memory is forward-phrased and atomic.** "Do X when Y because Z", never history. The kernel owns the envelope (id, created, `when`: the kinds, roles, skills and resources an item applies to). Recall is a deterministic policy over items and scope, ranked by specificity and by track record (items present in succeeded attempts rise). Experience (can be wrong, stale, deduped) and taste (the owner's preference, never wrong, broadly scoped) are different kinds.
15. **The ledger is the kernel's only state.** Runs, attempts, invocations, transitions, the pending queue, quota. Its backend is pluggable, and it may be partitioned by backend. Account quota shared by several harnesses is a ledger partition of append-only quota events: each harness appends its own consumption and folds the window at read time, so no harness takes a lock over another's account state. A quota store that needs the ledger's single-writer lock, or a second store under the ledger's name, breaks this principle. There is no kernel work store: domain state lives where the owner's adapter puts it, and a unit may have no store at all. (Shared quota ruled 2026-11-01 after generation 1.)
16. **Supply, store and scheduling are three pillars.** Suppliers produce units (folder, poll, webhook, schedule, operator). Stores hold unit state (one adapter may be both). The scheduler decides what runs next from pending units, lane WIP limits, capacity (runner slots, account eligibility) and a policy. Without a scheduler there is a library, not a harness.
17. **Human-in-the-loop is kernel.** Halting an attempt for an outside decision is universal. Who resolves it, through which surface, is not: the supervisor is one optional client of a control API made of operations, and operations (not capability strings) are what a client is granted.
18. **Metrics are queryable and honest.** Computed from ledger transitions, with sample counts beside every rate, so policy authors write exploration deliberately. Success is defined by the kind's terminal states, never by "the flow finished".

## Ergonomics standards

19. A first-time reader predicts what each line does from its name. Builders chain. Names are nouns for things and verbs for settings. Units sit in names or types (`budgetTokens`, `maxUsd`), never implied.
20. Full inference. Scenario code needs no `as`, `any`, `!` or `@ts-ignore`. A `.d.ts` that uses `any` to make inference "work" fails this standard.
21. Small surface. The fewest entities and methods that express the whole scenario battery without escape hatches. An entity with one use is suspect. A method nobody in the battery calls is removed.
22. No two words for one thing. Run, attempt, invocation, step have one definition each, or fewer words.


# Scenario battery

# Scenario 1: coding team

A product team's harness, the shape harness-dsl was first built for.

## Must express

- Three kinds of work in a hierarchy: Epic decomposes into Features; Bugs arrive on their own. Epic completes when its Features do. Feature and Bug share most of their lifecycle and handler but differ in how many build-and-audit rounds they get (Bug 3, Feature 5).
- Supply from three places at once for Bugs: an issue tracker (Linear), a folder of markdown files, and the operator typing to the supervisor. Features from the tracker and the operator. Epics from the tracker only.
- Bug and Feature state is kept in the tracker; the harness is not the source of truth for them.
- A builder agent on a worktree per attempt, with a file-lease guard (two attempts may not write the same file) and a stop check that runs the project's checks before the agent may stop.
- An auditor agent that finds deficits; the loop continues until none remain or rounds run out. The builder may halt the attempt for an owner decision.
- Accounts: three Claude subscriptions in a pool with per-account quota shares, drained soonest-expiring first, falling back to an API account. Model choice for the builder reads the ledger: use the cheaper model until its success rate on this kind of work, over 14 days and at least 20 samples, drops below 0.85.
- Memory: experience ("when touching payments, run the ledger fixture first, because the migration reorders rows") recalled by builder and auditor, recorded by the auditor; taste ("prefer early returns over nested conditionals") recalled by builder and planner, written by the owner.
- A service heartbeat every five minutes, all deterministic, whose failure creates a Bug through a trigger. The heartbeat flow must not reference the Bug kind.
- Scheduler: heartbeats first, then bugs, features, epics; a WIP limit of 2 concurrent bugs and 1 epic; starvation protection for features.
- Supervisor: a Claude Code session granted read and write on work, blocker resolution, memory writes, telemetry and account shares, plus one custom operation (a production health probe).
- Board and telemetry projections written as Markdown files.

## Hostile aspects

- The heartbeat kind must have no store and must still appear in telemetry.
- The same handler flow serves two kinds with different round counts without duplication.
- The model-choice policy must expose sample counts; a variant that hides them fails.

# Scenario 2: support triage

Customer conversations arrive from a helpdesk webhook. Nothing here touches files.

## Must express

- One kind of work, Conversation, supplied by a webhook (push) and by a periodic poll of the helpdesk for anything the webhook missed. State lives in the helpdesk via its API; the harness holds nothing but its ledger.
- Lifecycle: new, classifying, drafting, awaiting approval, sent, closed by customer, escalated. A human approves every outgoing reply (halt), except for a category the policy marks safe after 200 approved samples with zero rejections.
- Two agents: a classifier on a cheap model, a drafter on a stronger one. The drafter recalls taste (tone, phrases to avoid) and experience ("when the customer mentions a refund older than 30 days, cite policy 4.2"). A reviewer role (human, through the supervisor) records taste from its edits.
- Deadlines: each conversation carries an SLA; the scheduler orders by time to breach, not by arrival. A breached SLA fires a trigger that escalates (creates an Escalation unit in another lane with its own handler and a human-only flow).
- External cancellation: if the customer replies while a draft is awaiting approval, the attempt is cancelled and the unit returns to classifying with the new message.
- Per-unit cost ceiling: no conversation may spend more than $0.40 of model cost; a unit that would exceed it halts for a human.
- Metrics the policy reads: approval rate by category and by model, with sample counts.

## Hostile aspects

- Cancellation from outside an active attempt.
- A trigger whose source is time (SLA breach), not a transition.
- A cost ceiling scoped to a unit, not an account.
- A lane whose handler contains no model call at all (Escalation).

# Scenario 3: research pipeline

A team runs literature-style research: a topic goes in, a sourced report comes out.

## Must express

- Kind Topic, supplied by the operator and by a weekly schedule that re-opens topics tagged "recurring". Topics are stored in the harness's own store (no external system), so the first-party store is the right choice here.
- Handler: fan out 20 search-and-extract calls as one cloud batch on a cheap model (the batch API discount matters), gather, then one synthesis call on a strong model, then a deterministic citation check command that fails the attempt if a citation does not resolve.

Recall is still a deterministic policy; the vector store is a backend. Experience about sources ("when the source is a preprint server, downgrade confidence") is a second kind in a JSONL store.

- The synthesizer's model is chosen by a policy that compares two strong models on a metric the owner defines: citation-check pass rate.

## Hostile aspects

- A memory backend that is not a file and a recall policy that uses similarity, while recall stays deterministic.
- A cloud batch step inside a flow, priced at the batch discount in telemetry.
- Budget as a scheduling input (daily, across units).
- A terminal outcome, parked, that is neither success nor failure.

# Scenario 4: operations, no model anywhere

A platform team uses the harness purely as a durable scheduler of deterministic work. There is no model, no account, no agent in this harness. If a variant needs any of them to compile or start, it fails the scenario.

A Backup that succeeded but took over 2 hours records a note in a journal of operational experience, which is also a memory kind, even though nothing here reads memory into a prompt; the supervisor reads it.

- Observers: a Slack notification on every Incident transition, and the board file.

## Hostile aspects

- Zero model calls: every executable is a command.
- A trigger whose source is a pattern across several transitions.
- Preemption rules in the scheduler.
- A control API client that is plain HTTP.
- A memory kind with no agent reading it.

# Scenario 5: data job with approval

A nightly data job with one human gate in the middle and a retry policy.

## Must express

- Kind NightlyLoad, supplied by a schedule at 02:00, one unit per source system (four). State in the harness's store.
- Handler: extract (command, SSH runner), validate (command), then a model call that writes a plain-language summary of anomalies, then halt for a human to approve the load, then load (command), then verify (command).
- Retry: extract and load retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff on failure, as a policy on the step, not hand-written in the command. A validation failure does not retry; it halts for a human with the validation report.
- Outcome: loaded, loaded with warnings (verify found tolerable drift), rejected by the approver, or failed. Loaded with warnings is a success for scheduling purposes but must be distinguishable in metrics and on the board.
- A unit left waiting for approval past 09:00 is cancelled by a time trigger and a new one is not created until the next night.
- Resumability: if the harness process restarts while a unit is blocked on approval, the unit is still blocked after restart and resumes at the same step when approved.
- The approver works through the supervisor; the summary agent recalls taste about what the approver wants emphasised.

## Hostile aspects

- Retry with backoff as a declared policy on a step.
- Restart survival of a blocked attempt.
- A success-with-warnings outcome that is success to the scheduler and distinct to metrics.
- A time trigger that cancels, scoped to one kind.

- Curation operations on memory (merge, drop) exposed to the supervisor.
- A metric defined by the owner from recorded operator actions, not from attempt outcomes.

The owner runs two independent product harnesses (two repositories, two ledgers, two supervisors) that share the same three Claude subscription accounts.

# Scenario 8: lifecycles that do not fit

Three kinds of work chosen to break a pending/active/succeeded/failed/cancelled skeleton. A variant must express them without lying: mapping an outcome onto a skeleton state it does not mean is a failure of this scenario.

## Must express

- **Experiment**: an A/B test unit runs for two weeks, collecting a metric from a command every hour. It ends in one of: A wins, B wins, inconclusive. None of these is failure. The scheduler must treat all three as terminal; metrics must distinguish them; a policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how often are experiments inconclusive?"
- **Tenancy**: a customer's tenancy is a unit of work that is never terminal while the customer is a customer. It is re-evaluated monthly (usage review, a model-written summary, a human decision to upsell or not) and may be suspended and reinstated any number of times. It ends only on churn, which is neither success nor failure. The scheduler must not consider an active tenancy as occupying capacity between evaluations.
- **Negotiation**: a procurement negotiation unit alternates between the harness (an agent drafts the next offer) and the outside world (the vendor replies, via a webhook supplier that updates an existing unit rather than creating one). It may end in agreement, walk-away by us (a decision, not a failure), walk-away by them, or expiry (a time trigger). Each attempt is one round; the unit outlives many attempts.

## Hostile aspects

- Terminal states that are neither success nor failure, needed by metrics.
- A unit that is active for years and must not hold capacity.
- A supplier that updates an existing unit instead of creating one.
- An attempt-per-round model where the unit's identity spans attempts and external replies.
- If the variant changes the skeleton (adds outcomes, replaces the five with something else), its design notes must say what success rate means afterwards.

# Scenario 9: a harness watching itself

The support harness of scenario 2 observes its own metrics and acts on them. Nothing here is new work from outside; every unit created here is created by the harness about itself.

## Must express

- A trigger whose source is a metric threshold: when the approval rate for a category over the last 7 days falls below 0.9 with at least 50 samples, the harness creates one Audit unit for that category in an `audits` lane with a human-only handler. While an Audit for that category is open, no second one is created, however many samples cross the threshold.
- The same crossing records a candidate experience item scoped to the drafter role and the category: "when drafting for {category}, recall the stricter phrasing, because approvals fell to {rate}".
- When the category's rate recovers above 0.95, the open Audit is cancelled. Below 0.9 and above 0.95 are two thresholds on purpose: the trigger fires on a crossing, once, not on every sample.
- A trigger that pauses the `conversations` lane when the harness's own model error rate over the last hour exceeds 0.2 with at least 20 invocations, and resumes it when the rate falls below 0.05. Paused means: nothing new starts in the lane, running attempts finish. Both the pause and the resume are recorded on the ledger and visible on the board, with the metric value that caused them.
- Each conversation's SLA can be extended by the reviewer through the supervisor. The breach timer moves with the new deadline; the old deadline never fires.
- A policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how many Audits were opened per category this month" and "how long was the lane paused in total".

## Hostile aspects

- A trigger source that is a metric, not a transition, a time or an external event; it still fires only from recorded ledger state and its firings are recorded.
- Hysteresis: two thresholds, one firing per crossing.
- Deduplication by a group key (the category), not by kind.
- A consequence that acts on a lane, not on a unit, and is itself a recorded, queryable fact.
- A timer whose deadline changes after it was armed.
